result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.eigen_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get eigenvector centrality for each node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L15751-L15858){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.eigen_centrality( max_iter=100, tol=1e-06, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Eigenvector centrality measures node importance based on connections to other important nodes. It's the principal eigenvector of the adjacency matrix, computed via power iteration: `x = λ⁻¹ · A · x` A node has high eigenvector centrality if it's connected to other nodes that themselves have high centrality. Unlike degree centrality, it accounts for the quality (not just quantity) of connections. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of iterations for convergence. [tol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-06]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence tolerance threshold. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name to store eigenvector centrality scores in the node DataFrame. If `None` (default), automatically uses `eigen_centrality`. Overwrites column if it already exists. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores in NDF and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to centrality scores. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Calculate eigenvector centrality in a star graph: ::: {#f081aee7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="hub") .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("hub", "A") .add_edge("hub", "B") .add_edge("hub", "C") ) graph.eigen_centrality(return_dict=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {3: 0.4411521780288614, 1: 0.6451001995513372, 4: 0.4411521780288614, 2: 0.4411521780288614} ``` ::: ::: The hub scores highest since it's connected to every other node, while the three spokes -- each connected only to the hub -- end up with equal, lower scores. Store as node attributes and chain other operations: ::: {#9135599a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="hub") .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge(source="hub", target="A") .add_edge(source="hub", target="B") .add_edge(source="hub", target="C") ) ( graph .eigen_centrality(attr_name="centrality") .rescale_node_attrs(node_attr_from="centrality", node_attr_to="size", range=[0.5, 2.0]) .describe() ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Number of nodes : 4 Number of edges : 3 Directed : False Density : 0.50 Average degree (min, max) : 1.50 (1, 3) Connected : True Number of connected components : 1 Tree : True Bipartite : True Computations on nodes: - eigen_centrality() -> attr: 'centrality' (4 of 4 nodes) Node aesthetics: - size <- centrality via rescale (range: [0.5, 2.0]) (values: 0.5, 2.0, 4 of 4 nodes) ``` ::: :::
